text:
sara: FYI after the continuous-batcher tweak (token_budget target lowered) we’re seeing a small but sharp p95 spike on a few pools, +120ms on p95 and overall throughput down ~6% for two hours :grimacing:

infra-bot: ALERT p95 latency 365ms for model:redwood-7b pool:dedicated-eu (metric rule: cpu_latency_p95 > 300ms)

mike: ack. which rollout wave? full or 10% canary?

sara: rolled to 30% yesterday at 02:00UTC. canary looked fine for ~2h then drifted. the drift aligns with an uptick in small-shape batches (shape <= 8 tokens) causing kernel fallback logs to spike.

jin: got a short log dump? the kernel fallback path has a known slow-path for tiny batches on A100 kernel v2.1.

sara: pasted a trimmed snippet from runtime logs:```
[2026-03-17T02:34:12Z] batch formed: shape=(1,6,8), token_budget=32 -> kernel_choice=generic_fp32_slow
[2026-03-17T02:34:12Z] kvcache: evict_count=14, prefix_hits=0.03 -> increased eviction latency
[2026-03-17T02:34:13Z] request_ms=420 p95_window=300ms -> recording fallback
```

kyle: interesting — if small batches are more frequent, the heuristic that packs by token budget might oversplit and pick a conservative kernel. Could be a threshold tuning issue between pack_by_tokens and pack_by_shape.

ana: (typo, ana) we should check kernel selection histogram + batch shape time-series. if kernel selection switches at shape threshold 8 that matches the logs.

mike: can we repro with the perf client? run a mixed-shape synthetic with the new heuristic flag off vs on. command I use: `./perf/client --model redwood-7b --profile mixed --rps 200 --shapes 1,6,12,64`

sara: running that now in eu-dedicated-staging. also enabling `--trace-kernel-decisions` to get the full decision bag. will paste trace link when done. :eyes:

infra-bot: NOTE new alert suppressed for 15m; pager escalation avoided (auto-mitigation: scale-out + revert transient microburst config)

jin: quick theory: lowering token_budget target reduced the target batch size, causing more small-batch instances that trigger kernel `generic_fp32_slow`. Also KV cache eviction rate increased because we’re not reusing prefixes long enough (smaller batches => shorter KV lifetimes). net effect: per-token cost ↑ and p95 ↑.

kyle: sounds plausible. two quick experiments: 1) temporarily raise token_budget to previous value for the affected rollout wave; 2) tighten shape-to-kernel mapping so shape<=8 uses `smallfast` kernel if available. which is safer?

sara: I prefer 1 first (config-only rollback) — simpler and fast. if that fixes it we know the budget target was the lever.

ana: I'll open a quick rollout to flip `continuous_batching.token_budget=old_value` for 30% -> monitor 20m. if green, scale to 100% revert.

mike: also add temporary metric `batch_shape_rate{<=8}` to Grafana and alert if > 10% of total. helps future tuning.

jin: FYI I looked at a flame graph from the synthetic run (link: https://perf.internal/runs/2143658700/trace). notable time in `kernel_generic_dispatch` when shape<=8.

sara: synthetic results: with token_budget=old -> p95 back to baseline, throughput restored. with new token_budget -> reproduces +120ms p95.

kyle: good root cause then. follow-ups: (a) update heuristic to include a min_shape merge (if batch token sum < X and count < Y, prefer shape-coalescing), (b) add KV retention tweak to avoid premature eviction for rapid small-prefix reuse, (c) add a canary that slowly ramps token_budget changes with shape-metric gating.

ana: I’ll file a short RFC for (a) and (b) and include the perf numbers + logs. tagging eng-runtime-owners.

mike: thanks. for immediate mitigation we’ll revert token_budget for that rollout and watch for alerts. Sara — can you confirm when the config flip is live?

sara: flipped at 03:05UTC, metrics already show p95 back to baseline at 03:22UTC. keeping the 30% rollout paused until RFC accepted. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: RESOLVED alert for p95 latency model:redwood-7b pool:dedicated-eu at 03:25UTC

mike: nice work team. follow-up action items in the RFC: include a small A/B that measures kernel_choice distribution so we can detect these selection swings early.

jin: adding a small unit test to the kernel selector that exercises tiny-shape boundary and ensures preferred kernel is still chosen under token-budget perturbations. will PR today.

ana: thanks — closing the loop once RFC and PR land.

sara: one last note: logs show a handful of client requests with unusual prefix churn (clients doing many short-chats). ops might want to reach out to the affected customer if this recurs.

mike: good point — tagging support to be ready.

(ends)
